blindSummary: No criminalisation of trans presence. The unit's legislature created an administrative legal gender recognition procedure in a 2022 Civil Code reform; after the country's supreme court struck down its adults-only limit in June 2023, a new reform passed in 2024 extended recognition to children and adolescents. In May 2022 the legislature also added a penal-code chapter criminalising crimes against sexual orientation, gender identity and expression. The counterweight is the largest border city: the unit's attorney general publicly warned of a serial killer of women in prostitution there (at least 3 victims; suspect arrested July 2023 after an international police-cooperation notice and a federal investigative agency's assistance), only 22 of 278 killed women in the unit were classed as feminicides, and a 2021 burning of a trans woman's body in her home in that city is recorded within that pattern. Mixed: protective law, under-counted lethal risk concentrated in one border city.
blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation's unit-by-unit tracker on legal gender recognition in the country (March 2025), covering which of the 32 units have legislated an administrative procedure and the supreme court rulings that drove expansion. For this unit: a 2022 Civil Code reform created an administrative legal gender recognition procedure for adults; the country's supreme court invalidated its 18-years requirement in June 2023; a 2024 reform followed.

An international human-rights organisation's report (6 March 2024) on a neighbouring unit: no legal gender recognition procedure there exposes trans people to institutional mistreatment - the August 2023 killing of a local activist remained unsolved, hate-motivation provisions are absent from that unit's criminal code, and healthcare staff routinely out patients by calling legal names. Baseline for how a non-reforming unit behaves.

A global report (24 July 2024) on the capital city making transfemicide a crime with sentences up to 70 years (a law named after a trans woman murdered in an unsolved case, approved 18 July 2024), in one of the region's deadliest settings for trans people; over 95% of homicides nationally went unpunished in 2022.
blindTangential: The border-city serial-killer pattern centred on people in sex work - victims' gender-nonconforming presentation is part of the targeting, so it reads as bias-adjacent violence, not pure criminal opportunity.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2022/2024 legal gender recognition reforms and the penal-code hate-crime chapter operate on resident documents and prosecutions.
